title: Hazel and the Terminal
premise: August Winterbourne, a disgraced terraformer hiding under a false name in the colony ship Perpetual Spring, has spent ten years hauling cargo through contested orbits while tending a seed vault garden meant for settlers not yet born. When the colony's children begin sharing an identical dream—a garden singing in dead space—August recognizes the signal as a distress call from Terminal, an abandoned relay he helped build, and the only place the children's dream can originate. As the colony council moves to purge the 'infected' children and a rival faction races to weaponize the signal, August must choose between his anonymity, his duty to the children who trust him, and his love for Dr. Sefa Idris, the colony's physician who is ordered to report him. Racing the collapsing relay's final transmission window, August reaches Terminal, discovers the dream is the uploaded consciousness of the terraforming crew he abandoned a decade ago, and must decide whether to merge with them to save the children or stay human and let the signal die. He chooses a third path: broadcasting the crew's memories openly, sacrificing his hidden identity and his chance to return, so the colony can finally grieve—and so the children's garden can grow.
about_author: Paloma Underhill is the pen name of a former orbital logistics analyst who spent six years drafting manifests for stations that never launched. She writes about people who keep systems running and the quiet cost of being indispensable.

chapters.title: Cargo for the Unborn
chapters.summary: August's POV. He hauls nutrient pallets through contested orbit while tending the seed vault garden at shift's end. Establishes his routine, his false papers, and his tenderness toward plants over people. Emotional beat: loneliness disguised as competence.

chapters.title: The Children Who Dream Alike
chapters.summary: Dr. Sefa Idris, POV. Eleven children describe the same dream—a garden singing in the dark. Sefa logs it as mass suggestion, but one child draws a relay station she's never seen. Emotional beat: unease blooming into wonder.

chapters.title: Manifest Discrepancies
chapters.summary: August's POV. Council auditor Voss flags August's cargo routes as impossible—someone has been rerouting supplies toward dead space for months. August suspects a saboteur; the reader suspects August's own autopilot. Emotional beat: paranoia tightening.

chapters.title: Sefa's Examination
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. She scans the dreaming children and finds synchronized neural patterns no infection can explain. The children call the dream 'the garden that waits.' Sefa begins to believe them. Emotional beat: scientific certainty cracking.

chapters.title: Ten Years of Silence
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter, August's POV. Ten years ago, August's terraforming crew uploaded their minds into relay Terminal to seed a dead world. August fled before the upload, taking a new name. Emotional beat: guilt as a physical weight.

chapters.title: The Purge Order
chapters.summary: Councilor Voss's POV. Voss declares the dream a cognitive contagion and orders the children quarantined. Sefa protests; Voss hints she'll be next. Emotional beat: institutional fear hardening into cruelty.

chapters.title: Night Shift Confession
chapters.summary: August and Sefa's shared POV, alternating. Sefa confronts August with the children's drawing of Terminal—his old station. He admits nothing, but she sees the recognition. Emotional beat: two guarded people circling the same wound.

chapters.title: The Signal Strengthens
chapters.summary: Multiple brief POVs. The dream spreads to thirty children and two adults; comms pick up a carrier wave from dead space that shouldn't exist. Emotional beat: dread and awe entwined.

chapters.title: What August Buried
chapters.summary: August's POV. He digs out his old crew badge and the Terminal access key he swore to destroy. A memory: his crewmate Imani begging him to stay for the upload. Emotional beat: the past refusing to stay buried.

chapters.title: Quarantine Ward
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. The children, separated, dream harder—proof the dream isn't airborne but addressed. One girl, Noor, tells Sefa: 'The garden knows your name too.' Emotional beat: tenderness under surveillance.

chapters.title: Voss's Bargain
chapters.summary: Voss's POV. Voss offers August immunity in exchange for locating the signal source—she wants to weaponize or monetize it. August realizes she suspects who he is. Emotional beat: a trap dressed as mercy.

chapters.title: The Long Haul
chapters.summary: August's POV. He plots a cargo run to dead space under a maintenance pretext, needing Sefa to falsify medical clearances for the 'quarantined' children as cover. Emotional beat: crossing the line from hiding to acting.

chapters.title: Complicity
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. Sefa forges the clearances, knowing it ends her career. She and August admit, obliquely, that they've been watching each other for years. Emotional beat: love confessed through conspiracy.

chapters.title: Departure Window
chapters.summary: August's POV. Launch through contested orbit; a patrol nearly boards them. Noor and three other children stow away, having dreamed the route. Emotional beat: panic giving way to resolve.

chapters.title: The Dreaming Hold
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. In the cargo hold, the children teach August the dream's song—he realizes he already knows the melody from Terminal's calibration tones. Emotional beat: the past singing back.

chapters.title: Dead Space
chapters.summary: August's POV. The ship crosses into the silent zone where comms die and the dream becomes constant, shared even by August. He hears Imani's voice. Emotional beat: terror softening into homecoming.

chapters.title: Voss Follows
chapters.summary: Voss's POV. Voss commandeers a fast patrol ship, taking Sefa 'into protective custody.' She reveals she knows August is August Reyes, the deserter. Emotional beat: the hunter's own desperation exposed.

chapters.title: Terminal Approach
chapters.summary: August's POV. The relay appears—overgrown with engineered flora, the uploaded crew having terraformed their own prison. The children weep with recognition. Emotional beat: awe at beauty grown from abandonment.

chapters.title: Imani's Garden
chapters.summary: August's POV inside the dream. Imani's uploaded consciousness greets him—not with anger but with the ten years of growing they did without him. Emotional beat: forgiveness he hasn't earned, offered anyway.

chapters.title: The Dying Signal
chapters.summary: August's POV. Terminal's core is failing; the upload has weeks, not years. The dream was a plea: someone must carry the garden's memory back before the relay dies. Emotional beat: urgency sharpened by grief.

chapters.title: Sefa's Captivity
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. Aboard Voss's ship, Sefa convinces the patrol crew—many have children who dream—to mutiny. Emotional beat: quiet courage spreading like the dream itself.

chapters.title: The Merge Offer
chapters.summary: August's POV. The crew offers August the choice they once offered: upload and become the garden's keeper forever, saving the signal at the cost of his body and self. Emotional beat: temptation of erasure as penance.

chapters.title: Noor's Question
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Noor asks August why the garden needs him to disappear. Her simple logic plants the seed of a third option. Emotional beat: a child's clarity cutting through adult despair.

chapters.title: Voss Arrives
chapters.summary: Voss's POV. Voss docks at Terminal, takes the children hostage, and demands the upload technology. The garden's defenses—engineered roots—respond to the children's song. Emotional beat: power meeting something it can't command.

chapters.title: Root and Ruin
chapters.summary: August's POV. The station's flora disarms Voss's crew without harming them; Voss, confronted with Imani's recorded last words, wavers. Emotional beat: an enemy cracked open by grief.

chapters.title: Imani's Truth
chapters.summary: Imani's POV (dream-space). Imani reveals the upload was meant to be temporary—a bridge until the colony could join them—and August's flight left them alone with eternity. Emotional beat: accusation and absolution in one breath.

chapters.title: The Choice Reframed
chapters.summary: August's POV. August realizes the crew doesn't need a new keeper—they need to be remembered. He proposes broadcasting Terminal's full memory archive to the colony instead of merging. Emotional beat: hope built from refusal.

chapters.title: The Broadcast Gamble
chapters.summary: August's POV. The dying relay can transmit once. Voss, changed, offers her ship's antenna array to piggyback the signal. Emotional beat: unlikely alliance forged in the eleventh hour.

chapters.title: Sefa's Crossing
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. Sefa's mutinied patrol reaches Terminal. She and August finally speak plainly—about the years, the lie, the love. Emotional beat: intimacy after long siege.

chapters.title: Countdown
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. Terminal's core begins cascade failure early. The children sing the calibration song to stabilize it while August wires the broadcast. Emotional beat: collective effort against the clock.

chapters.title: The Window Opens
chapters.summary: August's POV. Transmission begins: ten years of the crew's memories, the garden, the song, the truth about August's flight. Emotional beat: exposure as liberation.

chapters.title: What the Colony Heard
chapters.summary: Colony POV, mosaic of voices. The broadcast reaches every sleeper on the Perpetual Spring. Grief, fury, and recognition ripple through the ship. Emotional beat: a community forced to feel at once.

chapters.title: Core Collapse
chapters.summary: August's POV. Terminal begins to die. The crew's consciousness, now mirrored in the broadcast, begins to let go—choosing completion over persistence. Emotional beat: farewell without bitterness.

chapters.title: The Merge Refused, Then Accepted
chapters.summary: August's POV. The relay offers August one final merge to carry a fragment of Imani home in his own mind. He accepts—not erasure, but companionship. Emotional beat: sacrifice transformed into gift.

chapters.title: Evacuation
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. The children, August, and the crew abandon Terminal as it burns green in dead space. Noor carries a seed pod from Imani's garden. Emotional beat: exodus with something saved.

chapters.title: Return Through Contested Orbit
chapters.summary: August's POV. The patrol and cargo ship run the gauntlet home; Voss publicly confirms August's identity and, to everyone's shock, defends him. Emotional beat: judgment rendered by the changed.

chapters.title: The Hearing
chapters.summary: August's POV. The colony tribunal weighs ten years of desertion against the broadcast's gifts. Sefa testifies; the children sing. Emotional beat: accountability met with grace.

chapters.title: Groundbreaking
chapters.summary: Shared POV. The colony opens its first true surface greenhouse, planting Imani's seed pod. The children's dream fades—replaced by a garden they can touch. Emotional beat: mourning completed into growth.

chapters.title: What August Carries
chapters.summary: August's POV. August, restored to his real name, tends the greenhouse with Sefa. Imani's fragment speaks in his dreams now—not a haunting, a conversation. Emotional beat: peace earned, not granted.

chapters.title: The Garden That Waits No More
chapters.summary: Noor's POV, years later. Noor, now an apprentice terraformer, ships out toward a new dead world carrying the archive. The last line mirrors the first: cargo for the unborn. Emotional beat: the cycle continued, consciously.
